Published as a student institution, not as an employer.

affiliations.research_notes: The Congressional Record explicitly says Osborne resigned his state job in 1942 to work for OSS. His signed state annual report documents the office, war-related federal leave, and November 6 resignation.

The 1941 yearbook identifies Helen Edith Osmun as a student; the Washington Post obituary independently gives her full maiden name, 1941 graduation, and wartime OSS analyst and translator service. This is an educational affiliation, not an employer claim.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Lithgow Osborne is confirmed as the New York Conservation Commissioner who resigned in 1942 to work for OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare exact name, state title, 1942 transition, and explicit OSS statement form a direct identity chain.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by an uncommon exact name in the index, a signed state report, and the Congressional Record's explicit OSS account.
claims.temporal_assessment: Both sources document the same 1942 transition.

claims.claim_text: Lithgow Osborne's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the New York State Conservation Department, where he served as Conservation Commissioner.
claims.evidence_excerpt: resigned his state job in 1942 to work for the Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Congressional Record gives an explicit departure-to-OSS sequence, while the state report documents his office and resignation.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the rare exact name and consistent title and chronology in official sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate transition in 1942; the signed state report supplies the November 6 resignation date.
claims.match_notes: This is classified as a government assignment, not private employment.

claims.claim_text: The New York State Conservation Department is the documented last civilian government employer before Lithgow Osborne entered OSS work.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The sources identify no intervening affiliation between his state resignation and OSS work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed identity in two official sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit departure from the state job to OSS in 1942.
claims.match_notes: The site keeps this field separate from immediate affiliation even though the same organization answers both questions here.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Helen Osmun is linked at high confidence to Helen Edith Osmun Parker, the Swarthmore graduate and wartime OSS analyst and translator.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The obituary supplies the exact maiden name, 1941 graduation, and OSS role; the contemporary yearbook independently prints the full name.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the uncommon exact maiden name and a direct OSS bridge in a reputable obituary, corroborated by a contemporary yearbook.
claims.temporal_assessment: The yearbook and obituary place graduation in 1941 before wartime OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The obituary's unrelated later-life details and living-relative information are excluded.

claims.claim_text: Helen Edith Osmun was a student at Swarthmore College and graduated in 1941 before her wartime OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The contemporary yearbook lists her full name, and the obituary supplies the graduation year and subsequent OSS role.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for the same uncommon full maiden name.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar education; neither source says the college was her immediate predecessor to OSS.
claims.match_notes: Swarthmore is published as a student affiliation and is not counted as an employer.
